research_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — selected building remains distinct from campus
research_updates.notes: The inventory target is one 315,400-square-foot building footprint named Facebook Altoona Data Center 1, while operator, IEDA, city, tax and DNR sources overwhelmingly describe the multi-building Siculus/Meta Altoona campus. Facebook announced the project April 23, 2013 and reported the Altoona data center online November 14, 2014. Assessor PIN 792310401005 contains ATN1, ATN2, ATN3, ATN4, ATN-4B and security sections; ATN1 is 312,131 square feet, close to but not equal to the IM3 footprint. It is retained only as a candidate crosswalk, so every campus, parcel and company-county amount remains unallocated. Siculus is a Facebook subsidiary and Facebook's corporate rename to Meta is operator continuity, not a predecessor transfer.

research_updates.title: State incentive and compliance audit — two awards retained without summation
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: IEDA FY2025 annual report, earlier IEDA data-center incentive table, indexed IEDA county reports, Siculus contract numbers 13-HQJTC-040 and 19-HQJPTC-025, award/completion dates, contracted capital investment, maximum tax benefit, reported jobs and total project cost at completion. Contract 13's maximum benefit is a ceiling, not realized credits; contract 19 reports zero maximum benefit. The historical $18 million/$299.5 million version of contract 13 is superseded by the current $26 million/$699.5 million table. No claims-paid, credits-certified, sales/use-tax refund, benefit-disbursement, wage-compliance detail, building allocation, or award-overlap reconciliation was found.

research_updates.title: Utility and infrastructure audit — tariff and franchise models tested, bills absent
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: Altoona utility, council-minutes and code records, infrastructure and will-serve amendments, water/sewer materials, MidAmerican's filed Iowa tariffs, and Siculus/Meta meter, demand, electricity, franchise-fee, pump-station and reimbursement paths. Meta's actual 2020-2024 kWh deterministically convert to annual average load of 111.872146, 108.527968, 119.133105, 141.929909 and 180.486339 MW (2024 uses 8,784 hours); those conversions are retained separately in modeled synthesis. MidAmerican offers materially different Large General Service, Substation Service and Individual Customer Rate structures, with demand, voltage, ratchet, rider, curtailment and possible special-contract terms. Average demand is a lower bound on peak billing demand but supplies no finite upper bound; therefore neither total electricity expense nor the associated franchise-fee base is bounded by annual kWh. Indispensable missing inputs are the service tariff/class or contract, monthly interval/billed kW, voltage and meter count, power factor, riders, bill totals, and customer-specific franchise inclusion, exemption/credit and remittance records. No tariff-cost or franchise-fee estimate is retained. The $500,000 pump-station commitment remains prospective because no completion, invoice or payment record was found.

The final air permit supports 112 permitted emergency engines across ATN and PCI groups; no engine is allocated to the selected building and permit limits are not actual emissions or generation. No site-specific discharge, fuel-use, actual-emissions, generator-run-hour, water-payment, wastewater-payment, or construction-water allocation was found.

research_updates.title: Workforce, procurement and supplier audit — hours and contractor identities found, spend absent
research_updates.notes: The reopened workforce and supplier trail covered Turner, IES Communications, Allied Construction Services, City permit reports, bid and procurement indexes, claims/check-register and lien queries, Hardhat in Hand/DMACC training, and recipient records. Meta names Turner, reports seven training graduates, and reports 8.7 million construction work hours since 2013; Iowa WARN identifies an IES event at 500 Share Way, and OSHA identifies Allied at 100 Share Way. Dividing 8.7 million hours by a 2,080-hour convention yields 4,182.692307692308 standardized FTE-year equivalents, retained only as labor-time equivalence—not unique workers, observed FTE, Iowa-resident employment or a selected-building result. Applying IEDA's $23.12 and $53.87 qualifying-job wage commitments yields $201.144 million and $468.669 million, with a $334.9065 million midpoint; this is retained as benchmark sensitivity, not observed payroll or a statistical/true-value bound. A 400-person operating scenario times 2,080 hours and the same wage anchors yields $19.23584 million, $32.02784 million midpoint and $44.81984 million, also retained only as sensitivity because daily people are not annual FTEs and may mix employees/contractors. Indispensable inputs remain certified payroll, trade/hour distributions, annual average employee and contractor FTE, benefits, residence, occupation mix, supplier invoices and local-purchase shares. Supplier contribution remains unsupported; payroll scenarios are modeled separately with all limitations.

research_updates.title: Expansion, adjacent project and continuity audit — phases kept separate
research_updates.notes: Sources checked: operator announcements from 2013-2026, local permit reports, DNR ATN/PCI equipment labels, Siculus corporate identity, and reporting for adjacent Polk County data-center construction. Operator sources describe at least seven expansions and a campus expected to exceed five million square feet; permit records specifically identify later ATN 5/6 work. No evidence supports treating all later buildings, adjacent confidential projects, regional wind generation, or every Siculus parcel as the selected original building. Corporate sources support Facebook-to-Meta/Siculus continuity, so no predecessor asset transfer or pre-acquisition baseline is inferred.

research_updates.title: Fiscal and public-cost audit — real-property payments found; net account still unbounded
research_updates.notes: The correction establishes separate actual 2020-2024 real-property payment series for all 10 active Siculus PINs plus current taxable values and bills. Exact annual active-PIN sums are $1,321,478, $1,834,994, $1,846,260, $2,219,356 and $2,249,854; they are retained as modeled aggregation totals with all retired/successor terminal bills excluded and may not be added to component claims. The 2024 $2,249,854 total also defines the equal-cost annual local-service break-even threshold. That threshold is not observed cost or net fiscal benefit; missing PILOT, franchise, incentive-realization and public-cost series are the reason to publish the threshold, not a reason to omit it. The approximately $810,000 temporary-building PILOT remains a projection with no receipt; the $500,000 pump-station commitment has no completion/payment record; IEDA's $26 million maximum remains a ceiling; and the reported 2019 PILOT/abatement/franchise terms lack a realized city ledger. Exact Siculus/Facebook/Meta searches found no named row among 332 Altoona TIF-expenditure or 475 Altoona urban-renewal rows, which does not prove zero unnamed or non-TIF cost. No realized public-service-cost dollar record or net fiscal result is asserted.

research_updates.title: County-statistics audit — two treatment dates and a screened Iowa donor pool tested
research_updates.notes: The governed 2001-2024 BLS QCEW employment/wage and BEA GDP panel was tested with construction-start treatment in 2013 and first-operation treatment in 2014. The candidate untreated pool is Linn, Johnson, Scott, Black Hawk, Woodbury, Dubuque and Story counties; Dallas and Pottawattamie were excluded for known hyperscale data-center exposure. The pool is explicit but not pre-registered, and Polk had Microsoft exposure by 2012 while Meta construction and later phases overlap. Results are retained only as design diagnostics, not contribution estimates.

research_updates.title: County outcome model decisions — pretrend, donor and treatment sensitivity tested separately
research_updates.notes: Using the seven-county unweighted pool and 2001-2012 preperiod, normalized-log-index RMSE / annual-growth correlation / pre-gap slope were: employment 0.0182 / 0.890 / -0.320% per year; nominal weekly wage 0.0245 / 0.648 / +0.008% per year; real GDP 0.0519 / 0.705 / -0.859% per year. Mean 2013-2019 post-versus-pre gaps were employment +2.547638%, wage -0.387495%, GDP +7.450688%; switching treatment to 2014 produced +3.099642%, -0.402464% and +10.169728%. Leave-one-donor-out ranges across both treatment specifications were employment +1.979955% to +4.260418%, wage -0.833174% to +0.111288%, and GDP +4.860594% to +13.547587%. Employment has good raw prefit but a nonflat pre-gap and overlapping 2013 construction/2014 operations/later expansions; GDP has weaker prefit, a material pretrend and treatment sensitivity; wage has a nearly flat pre-gap and a robust near-zero descriptive result, but county average composition, concurrent metro treatments and absent selected-building exposure prevent project attribution. Each diagnostic is retained as a low-confidence descriptive comparison-gap sensitivity, never as a Meta effect, causal result or selected-building contribution.

research_updates.title: Contribution-account disposition — second corrective candidate pending adversarial review
research_updates.notes: The second-corrected evidence fragment contains 100 records: 91 reported actuals and nine source projections, including two explicit IEDA qualifying-wage inputs. Together with the one existing baseline construction-peak record, the merged project has 101 direct records, 92 reported actuals and nine projections. The new modeled-synthesis fragment contains 17 estimates: five exact annual active-PIN tax aggregations, one 2024 equal-cost local-service threshold, five deterministic average-load conversions, one construction job-year equivalence, two payroll sensitivities and three descriptive county comparison gaps. All remain unallocated or not applicable to the selected building; aggregation notes prohibit adding modeled totals to component claims. Material gaps remain for selected-building allocation, personal property, ordinary tax distributions, PILOT/franchise receipts, realized incentives, audited payroll, supplier/local spending, observed public costs, tariff bills and causal county outcomes. The five exact water observations have a complete proposed metric/record/regression payload for orchestrator catalog reconciliation. This handoff supersedes both earlier zero-model conclusions, is candidate_corrected_round2_pending_adversarial_review, and is not accepted evidence.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Apple Mesa retains three narrowly scoped business-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals from its project fragment; Switch Citadel retains four exact fiscal arithmetic or break-even syntheses; Digital Crossroad Hammond retains two two-account paid-tax arithmetic or break-even syntheses from its project fragment. Reported observations, forecasts, and remaining models stay separate. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00116005354: Post-audit last-resort modeling gate for Apple Maiden. No estimate survives: campus and company/county evidence cannot be allocated to IM3 building 00116005354, annual incentive observations have unresolved municipal and service-cost gaps, contractor identities lack spend and geography, employment snapshots lack payroll and residence, and county aggregates lack a defensible treatment share or counterfactual. The direct-evidence fragment records every candidate-specific rejection and leaves unresolved metrics as gaps rather than fabricating building shares, tax receipts, utility use, multipliers or causal effects. prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Last-resort NAP7 modeling pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact, same-property-account fiscal-year 2027 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed property-tax bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, resource, community and county outcome candidates were rejected because compatible NAP7 inputs or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Last-resort Markley Lowell model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact same-account FY2026 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed four-quarter real-property bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, fiscal-net, resource, community and each GDP, employment and wage candidate are rejected separately in the evidence fragment because compatible inputs, scope alignment, non-overlap proof or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00300974499: Corrective policy-1.3.0 synthesis. Three legacy combined real-and-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals are superseded by narrower business-personal-property-only estimates because the Apple BPP account directly exhibits the 5% assessment ratio while the real-property account has a different valuation base. The replacements hold observed effective tax rates and full cash value constant and isolate only the assessment-ratio component; they are not cash grants, audited forgone-revenue amounts or net fiscal benefits. All other legacy Apple Mesa estimates fail the direct-evidence, scope, time-profile, geography or decision-relevance gates and are marked for removal in the evidence fragment. prj_study_im3_building_00359930465: Post-fifth-pass last-resort modeling gate for Equinix Seattle SE3 retains eight bounded syntheses. Construction is represented separately by the AGC/DJC $50 million-$100 million award-category sensitivity and a 50,482-hours wage benchmark; neither is audited spend or certified payroll. Opening evidence for 24-hour operations and security supports only a conditional one-active-post coverage floor and wage-cost benchmark, not observed posts, headcount, payroll or total staffing. The 2011 lease's up-to-9-MW allocation remains a 25/50/100-percent throughput sensitivity, with separate statewide/tariff price and eGRID NWPP location-based emissions benchmarks that are not bills, measured emissions or market-based results. A medium-confidence identity sets the 2026 same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold equal to the exact landlord-parcel bill; it does not estimate actual public cost, tenant pass-through, cash receipt, recipient distribution or net fiscal impact. A supplier/non-labor residual is rejected because the award category does not define cost coverage and the reported hours do not establish complete labor coverage; community and causal county-effect candidates still fail for lack of compatible inputs or identification. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00388148510: Project-scoped modeled synthesis for TierPoint Little Rock. Eleven resolved-year real-property taxable values are multiplied by signed code 03/33 school, city, and county millage components; 2025 is excluded because its observed Amount Due does not disclose the underlying revised taxable value. A conditional zero-leave FTE-equivalent floor translates the facility-specific 2012 onsite NOC staffed 24/7/365 statement without claiming employee headcount or payroll. Two low-confidence engineering sensitivities use one, not both, of the redundant 3,000 kVA utility transformers and expose hypothetical power-factor, utilization, and PUE assumptions. Every estimate is modeled_not_observed_or_audited and excluded from sourced-record counts, cash receipts, realized-benefit totals, and net-fiscal claims. prj_study_im3_building_00397914434: Corrective last-resort modeling pass for Apple Prineville. Five narrow, unallocated syntheses now survive: a same-land-account tax-payment break-even identity; a 2018 campus/company payroll sensitivity anchored to the reported 100 jobs and three official BLS Central Oregon occupation benchmarks; FY2025 campus electricity-cost sensitivity using EIA Oregon customer-class averages after PacifiCorp direct-access tariffs proved noncomputable from public inputs; deterministic FY2025 average-load conversion; and an EPA eGRID location-based electricity-emissions factor sensitivity. None is allocated to IM3 building 00397914434. The cost range is not Apple's bill, the payroll range is not observed payroll, and the emissions range is not Apple's market-based Scope 2 result and preserves Apple's 100 percent renewable-electricity claim. Investment, construction, supplier, community, net-fiscal and causal county-outcome candidates remain rejected for missing scope-compatible inputs or identification. prj_study_im3_building_00438078069: Second corrective modeled-synthesis pass for Meta Altoona. Exact annual active-account property-tax aggregations and the 2024 equal-cost public-service threshold implement study-modeling-policy 1.3.0; deterministic average-load conversions, labor-hour equivalence, explicitly stylized payroll sensitivities, and noncausal county comparison gaps retain every input and overlap limitation. All results remain unallocated to the selected 315,400-square-foot IM3 building. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00472761713: Third-pass modeled synthesis for NYSE Group's U.S. Liquidity Center in Mahwah. project_description: Meta's Altoona project is an operating multi-building data-center campus in Altoona, Polk County, Iowa, held in public records through its Siculus subsidiary. Facebook announced the project in April 2013 and reported the data center online on November 14, 2014; subsequent expansions extended construction into the 2020s. This account follows the selected 315,400-square-foot IM3 building footprint while keeping campus-wide investment, employment, utility, permit, incentive, and community figures unallocated from that building.
